items.title: The composite of two maps of admissible sequences is homotopic to zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file dga.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-nilpotent at source lines 840-867: for a dg algebra A, three admissible short exact sequences 0 -> K_i -> L_i -> M_i -> 0 indexed by i = 1,2,3, and maps b : L_1 -> L_2 and b' : L_2 -> L_3 whose two squares commute up to homotopy, the composite b' b is homotopic to zero. The proof at source lines 869-876 is short but it is the step that makes the maps of triangles rigid: it invokes the author's lemma on homotopy commutative squares twice, once for each square cum triangle, to replace b and b' by homotopic maps for which the relevant squares commute strictly, and then translates the strict commutativity into the two containments of images and kernels that force b' b to be the zero map of modules. The substance is the reduction from commuting up to homotopy to commuting on the nose, and the observation that the two containments make the composite vanish; the statement mentions neither. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
